hema: FYI I hit a confusing UX in the Go SDK while trying to wire streaming generators into our HTTP handler. The quickstart uses context.Background() and client.Close() and that pattern caused a flaky panic when a short-lived auth refresh happened concurrently.

 yves: Can you paste the minimal repro?

 hema: Sure. This is basically the quickstart verbatim: 

```go
ctx := context.Background()
c := redwood.NewClient(ctx, redwood.Opts{Model: "mini"})
it := c.Generator().Stream(ctx, "prompt")
for it.Next() { fmt.Print(it.Value().Text) }
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Println(err) }
```

Logs: panic: send on closed channel from gen/streamer.push in some runs. Repro: set TOKEN_TTL=2s and call c.Close() from another goroutine after ~1s while iterating.

 claire: Two problems: 1) using Background gives ambiguous ownership for long-lived clients in sample code; 2) token refresh path can replace token/transport mid-stream if we don't serialize it 9-> races.

 yves: UX suggestion: update quickstart to show request-scoped usage and explicit iterator ownership, e.g. handler binds generator to req.Context and defers it.Close() on the iterator rather than relying on client.Close. Also add a short explanation so users don't copy the Background anti-pattern.

 hema: Proposed sample change:
```go
func Serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  gen := redwood.NewGenerator(r.Context(), redwood.Opts{Model: "mini"})
  it := gen.Stream(r.Context(), "hi")
  defer it.Close() // iterator owns stream lifecycle
  for it.Next() {
    io.WriteString(w, it.Value().Text)
  }
}
```

 claire: On the SDK side I think we should: a) serialize token refresh (singleflight or mutex) so only one goroutine swaps transport; b) make iterator hold a stable transport reference until Close(); c) add an integration -race test that forces concurrent refresh + caller cancel.

 yves: Ergonomics question: should we change the public API to make Stream return a first-class Iterator type with Close() error and document client.Close() as process-shutdown only? That reduces accidental cross-effects. We can ship it as an additive type and keep the old helper as a compat shim.

 hema: That sounds reasonable. I'll open a tiny PR that: updates the quickstart sample + docs to show correct pattern, adds a TTL toggle repro script, and adds the integration test. I'll prototype the Iterator type in a follow-up behind a feature flag and file a parity ticket if we change surface.

 parity-bot: PARITY-78: If public surface changes are proposed, open a parity ticket and follow the checklist.

 ci-bot: Created INF-6021: "go sdk: streaming iterator ambiguous ownership leads to race with auth refresh". Attached repro and nightly -race job.

 claire: Also add a short DX note in the Go quickstart called "Streaming gotchas": avoid context.Background for request-bound generators, prefer iterator-owned Close, and show a token-refresh singleflight example.

 hema: Will do. Thanks all ":)"
